title: Hybrid warmup decay orchestrator and primer-schedule estimator
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Cold-starts and short-context sessions continue to dominate tail latency in our production traces. Existing warmup priming is static and either over-primes (wasting tokens) or under-primes (leaving kernels cold). This PR introduces a hybrid warmup orchestrator that combines a short lived aggressive primer for the first few requests and a decaying primer estimator that gradually reduces primer tokens as sequence history accrues. Design: 1) hybrid_warmup.py implements the orchestrator and a configurable schedule engine, supporting exponential and linear decay profiles; 2) a small estimator component computes an initial primer length based on recent session entropy and model tokenization characteristics; 3) primer caches are stored in a lightweight LRU keyed by session fingerprint with explicit TTLs to avoid warmup amplification; 4) a new decay_profile_reporter exports per-session warmup token counts, p95 latency delta vs baseline, and primer hit/miss ratios to the bench telemetry pipeline. Tests: unit tests for decay math and estimator heuristics, integration smoke in the bench harness against a 2-model local stack, and a deterministic replay test that asserts no worse than 3% regression on median latency for long sessions. Rollout plan: staged Canary via the perf-canary harness with traffic split 0.5/5/20/100 and automatic rollback on latency regression >5% at p95. Checklist: - [x] implement orchestrator and estimator - [x] add unit + integration tests - [x] wire reporter to bench telemetry - [x] update bench CI to include new smoke job - [x] documentation in bench/README describing config knobs - [x] add Linear tickets for follow-ups (ENG-2148, ENG-2213)
